summary: Log cabin with cupola on Freeman Peak, built in the early 1920s and destroyed in the mid-1950s; sources disagree on the dates.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in the mid-1950s; sources give 1954 or 1956

staffing.status: Known staff Frank Freeman (1919); no later staffing source found

facts.agency: Nez Perce National Forest (Bitterroot National Forest until 1957)

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as a hike-in; no source describes access today

events.note: Lookout Billie Hartman on Freeman's Peak, per a 1916 Idaho County Free Press item quoted by the Forest Lookouts site
Log cabin built near water; alidade placed on the peak
Cabin moved to the peak and a cupola added; a University of Idaho document gives 1923 as the build year
Log cabin with cupola built atop the south point, per three lookout sites
Forest Service list and one lookout-history site give 1954; Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give 1956
Administration transferred from Bitterroot National Forest to Nez Perce National Forest

The site's administration moved from the Bitterroot to the Nez Perce National Forest in 1957; the record names only the earlier forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The University of Idaho document gives 1923 for the log cabin with cupola, and one site says the cabin was moved and given a cupola in 1923. Three lookout sites give 1926 for a cabin with a cupola on the south point. Story reports both dates and does not choose between them.
The Forest Service list and one lookout-history site give 1954; Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give 1956. Story reports both; the event uses 1954 with the 1956 date in its note.

sources.title: Log Cabins with Cupolas, Nez Perce National Forest

notes_for_editor: Five sources, three of them lookout-history sites that overlap. Build and destruction dates conflict and the story gives both. Staffing has only the 1916 newspaper item and a 1919 name. The undated University of Idaho document is the only one that treats the remaining lookouts as a group. No source describes the site today or whether it is open to visitors.
